claim: The Citadelle is a 17th-century hexagonal keep (built 1602-1608) housing a maritime history museum across two floors with eleven ground-floor rooms on fishing and trade, plus exhibits on sailors Allard, Suffren and Bouchard, and offers one of the best coastal views.
quote: the dungeon of the Citadel of Saint-Tropez ... offers one of the most beautiful views of the coast ... eleven rooms covering local fishing, coastal trading, shipyards ... General Allard, the Bailli de Suffren, and Hippolyte Bouchard

claim: Citadelle de Saint-Tropez maritime museum admission is EUR 9 per person, with hours 10am-6:30pm April-September and 10am-5:30pm October-March.
quote: The entrance fee is EUR 9 per person ... April 1 to September 30: 10am-6:30pm; October 1 to March 31: 10am-5:30pm

claim: The Citadelle is closed for renovation works with reopening scheduled for 18 April 2026.
quote: La Citadelle is currently closed for works, with reopening scheduled for 18/04/2026

claim: The Musée de l'Annonciade, founded 1922 in a former chapel at Place Georges Grammont, holds works from 1890-1950 (Pointillist, Nabi, Fauve) by Signac, Cross, Matisse, Derain and Marquet, recalling the town's role as an avant-garde painting centre after Signac arrived in 1892.
quote: founded in 1922 ... one of the most active centers of avant-garde painting in the early 20th century ... Signac, Cross, Matisse, Derain, and Marquet

claim: Musée de l'Annonciade entry is EUR 5-6 full / EUR 3.50 reduced, free for under-12s, open Tuesday to Sunday roughly 10am-6pm (later in high summer).
quote: Full price is 5 to 6 €, reduced price is 3.50 € ... free entry for children under 12 ... open from Tuesday to Sunday

claim: La Ponche is the old fishing quarter of Saint-Tropez, a maze of narrow cobbled streets just off the Vieux Port and the town's most picturesque, atmospheric historic area.
quote: La Ponche ... the historic center of Saint-Tropez ... the most picturesque area of the city, with its colorful narrow cobbled streets

claim: The Vieux Port (Old Port) sits at the heart of town, lined with pastel Mediterranean townhouses, cafe terraces and moored yachts; the ochre Notre-Dame de l'Assomption bell tower (1634, restored 1980s) is the town's emblem above an 18th-century church with Italian-style interiors.
quote: ochre-and-sienna bell tower of Notre-Dame de l'Assomption is a defining feature of the Saint-Tropez skyline ... Originally built in 1634 and restored in the 1980s ... the 18th century, is a listed historic site with elegant Italian-style interiors

claim: Place des Lices is a shaded square near the Vieux Port where locals play petanque and which hosts a traditional Provencal market of fruit, vegetables and flowers on Tuesday and Saturday mornings.
quote: Place des Lices is a pleasant shady square ... where the elderly of Saint-Tropez gather to play petanque. On Tuesday and Saturday mornings, a traditional Provencal market takes place

claim: Brigitte Bardot's 1956 film And God Created Woman transformed Saint-Tropez from a sleepy fishing village into a jet-set destination; she bought the La Madrague residence in 1958, drawing stars like Mick Jagger and Eddy Barclay and making the town a jet-set party hub.
quote: And God Created Woman (1956) ... transformed the French Riviera town from a sleepy fishing village into a sizzling jet-set destination ... In 1958, Brigitte Bardot acquired the residence La Madrague ... Mick Jagger ... the international jet-set
